title.narrative: Increasing Community Resilience through Supporting Women’s Livelihoods in post-Earthquake in Homs - Syria

description.narrative:
Resilience in this context is closely linked to the empowerment of women's livelihoods in Homs. Empowering women economically by providing access to resources, tools, knowledge, and microfinance opportunities can foster resilience among not only women but the wider communities in Homs, while contributing to local economic recovery. Such initiatives can help break the cycle of dependency and vulnerability, allowing women to become active agents in their economic recovery and contributors to their communities' resilience. By focusing on women's economic empowerment and challenging restrictive social norms, efforts can not only mitigate the impacts of the aftermath of war but also lay the foundation for more inclusive and sustainable recovery and development in Homs after the fall of Assad’s regime.
Reflecting on the recent changes and challenges in Homs, Syria, SAWA proposes a strategy aimed at early recovery through a participatory approach that enhances gender integration in the workforce and community resilience. SAWA will support women-entrepreneurs who already had their livelihoods running before the earthquake and lost it due to it in Homs; providing them with advanced capacity-building and microfinancing to rebuild their businesses. In this project, SAWA aims to bridge the gap between humanitarian and relief interventions and development; In the medium- to longer term, the focus should shift towards the creation of more sustainable employment opportunities particularly after the fall of the Assad regime which poses opportunities for a stable environment that foster sustainable development and businesses. SAWA aims to do this by;
Enhancing the availability of information about the specific needs of Syrian entrepreneurs women in Homs
Enhancing women’s accessibility to resources through technical and soft capacities; and
Contributing to the resilience of livelihood systems of Syrian women coming from the targeted area.
